text:
emily: FYI hitting a reproducible parser crash in the JS onboarding sample when doing very tight abort+reconnect loops (~30-80ms). final [DONE] comes, then one more data line that contains a partial JSON and our parser throws.

jared: can you paste the raw stream fragment?

emily: sure — from a tcpdump against the dev proxy: 

data: {"seq":1,"text":"hi"}
data: {"seq":2,"text":"there"}
data: [DONE]
data: {"seq":2,"text":"!"}

leo: looks like the proxy is flushing a buffered packet after the server closed the chunked response. we toggled tcp_nodelay last sprint, wonder if that's related.

emily: quick workaround in sampleapp: swallow any data events after receiving [DONE] for that connection. stops the crash but feels like dodging the root cause.

jared: agree short-term client guard is fine. long-term we should either: (A) add monotonic chunk seq per event (breaks parity with minimal servers), (B) fix proxy ordering/flush behavior, or (C) make SDKs across languages ignore post-DONE fragments and emit a telemetry counter.

leo: i'm for B + C. infra will audit proxy flush semantics and we can add telemetry to quantify how often this happens in the wild.

emily: can we standardize the client guard across SDKs so sampleapp stays consistent?

jared: yes. i'll open a cross-SDK task: implement "drop events after DONE until new connection" with a small unit test in each SDK. also add an integration test in the sampleapp that simulates a late-flush from an intermediary.

infra-bot: Task created: DEVEX-891 - "SDK: guard against post-DONE SSE fragments; sampleapp e2e test" (assignee: jared)

leo: i'll follow up on proxy flags and add a short note to the onboarding README: "If you rapidly reconnect, intermediaries may replay buffered chunks; SDKs drop stray post-DONE events to avoid parse errors."

emily: thanks — saving new users a bunch of head-scratching.
